function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal authorization or instruction that gives a person or organization the authority to act on behalf of another party. In many contexts—especially in finance, law, and business—a mandate defines the scope, limits, and responsibilities of the authorized agent. Key aspects of a mandate include: | Aspect | Description | |--------|-------------| | **Parties involved** | • **Principal** – the person or entity granting authority.
• **Agent/Representative** – the person or entity receiving authority. | | **Scope of authority** | Specifies what actions the agent can take (e.g., signing contracts, making investment decisions). | | **Duration** | When the mandate starts and ends, or conditions that trigger its termination. | | **Limitations & restrictions** | Any constraints on the agent’s powers (e.g., maximum transaction amounts, types of permissible actions). | | **Reporting & accountability** | How the agent must report back to the principal and any oversight mechanisms. | | **Legal & regulatory compliance** | Ensures the mandate adheres to applicable laws and regulations. | Mandates are common in: - **Financial services** (e.g., investment mandates, payment mandates) - **Corporate governance** (e.g., board mandates, executive mandates) - **Legal representation** (e.g., power of attorney, legal mandates) - **Government & public administration** (e.g., mandates for public bodies) In short, a mandate is a clear, documented set of instructions that empowers an agent to act on behalf of a principal within defined boundaries.
